liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Iko Iko** (1 review): The Aiko Aiko was hot, according to the reviewer [15]
- **Picasso Moon** (1 review): Reviewer and a friend climbed to the bleachers to sit down during Picasso Moon [11]
- **Crazy Fingers** (1 review): Reviewer felt Crazy Fingers was missing a spark [11]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Band was playfully knocking Dark Star off its sacred-cow pedestal [13]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): The Dark Star tease inside Wharf Rat is singled out as excellent [11]

## The recordings

- **gd91-06-28.sbd.miller.11706.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 172 min; rated 3.63/5 by 27 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound quality is called impeccable, credited to David Gans's work; Reviewer found the sound system awful and the band's voices tired [13][20]
- **gd1991-06-28.150679.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 172 min [3]
- **gd1991-06-28.sbd.eD.9592.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 160 min [7]
- **gd1991-06-28.150645.sbd.pearson-healy.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 22 songs; 172 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [2]

## Around the show

- Carlos opened the show; the reviewer sat in the 22nd row, far over to the right [10]
- Mickey's facial expression during the show was memorable to the reviewer [14]
- Santana was busted for marijuana and played a lackluster opening set before the Dead came on [15]
- Reviewer saw huge amounts of LSD in the crowd while police focused on bootleg t-shirts [16]
- Some fans dosed people at random using squirt guns [16]
- Medics dragged out a dazed, grinning person from the crowd [16]
- Crowd felt scary and overly wild; reviewer recalls one or more people carried out on stretchers [17]
- People roamed with big super soakers dosing others, with a strong, scary acid vibe [18]
- June 1991 had a spark absent in the months before and after, with the band playful [13]
- Though full of overplayed songs, the band made familiar material sound fresh [14]
- Considered underrated, perhaps not the best of 1991; the band's only Mile High appearance [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd91-06-28.sbd.miller.11706.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> Dat> Samplitude> CD, Seed Supplied By David Gans [1]. Also: Charlie Miller transferred it using a Sony R500, Behringer SRC2000 and M-Audio Dio 2448 [1]
- **gd1991-06-28.150679.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  October 1, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [3]. Also: Tape flips and some tuning were patched using a master DAT soundboard [3]
- **gd1991-06-28.sbd.eD.9592.shnf**: transferred by eD; source: SBD (FM?)>DAT>CDR [7]. Also: Sector boundaries verified and shntool seekable SHN made by eD (efojr) on 05/24/02; Part of The Music Never Stopped Project, from seed discs provided by Paul [7]
- **gd1991-06-28.150645.sbd.pearson-healy.miller.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  October 1, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Worthpoint: [11x17" GRATEFUL DEAD and Santana Poster for the 1991 Denver MILE HIGH Stadium | #2052884451](https://www.worthpoint.com/worthopedia/11x17-grateful-dead-santana-poster-2052884451) [22]
- Fan art by Robbi Cohn: [1991-06-28 Mile High Stadium, Denver, CO, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1991-06-28-mile-high-stadium-denver-co-usa/) [23]
